corrections.was: Three axis drawings, one per engine, with the up axis in red. The up axis is the one that points up. Godot and Unity are Y-up, so height is the y value, and Unreal is Z-up, so height is the z value. Handedness is the other half of the setup. Unity and Unreal are left-handed, and Godot is right-handed. For example, a jump that raises the player's y value in Godot raises its z value in Unreal.
corrections.now: Three axis drawings, one per engine, with the up axis in red. The up axis is the one that points up. Godot and Unity are Y-up, so height is the y value, and Unreal is Z-up, so height is the z value. Handedness is the other half of the setup. Unity and Unreal are left-handed, and Godot is right-handed. For example, in a three D game, a jump that raises the player's y value in Godot raises its z value in Unreal.
corrections.why: Y-up is the three D convention; in Godot 2D, as in Walker (jump velocity minus three hundred twenty in tuning.gd, chapter 1), a jump lowers y, so the unscoped example taught the wrong direction for the course's own 2D games.

bookend_corrections.was: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. People moving from Godot to Unity often say a node is a component. It is not. A Godot node maps to a Unity GameObject, and a component is a piece added to it. The course ran only Godot, so the Unity and Unreal names come from their documentation. This film goes through the terms, each one shown with all three names.
bookend_corrections.now: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. People moving from Godot to Unity often say a node is a component. Not quite. A Godot node is one object, like a Unity GameObject. Where Unity adds components, Godot uses a node type and child nodes. The Unity and Unreal names come from their documentation, not from runs. This film goes through the terms, each one shown with all three names.
bookend_corrections.why: 'It is not [a component]' contradicts the node slide, whose Component row gives Godot's counterpart as 'node type and child nodes' (child nodes do a component's job; chapter 4's Unreal table maps node to 'Actor or Component'); and 'The course ran only Godot' contradicts chapter 1, which says the course used Unity and Unreal through Spring 2026.

bookend_corrections.now: one object, like a Unity GameObject
bookend_corrections.why: 'A Godot node is a Unity GameObject' is an identity the slide does not make: its Node row defines node, GameObject and Actor as 'One object in the scene', while its picture shows the Godot player as 3 nodes against 1 GameObject with 3 components; 'one object, like a Unity GameObject' is the smallest statement the slide supports.
